Consumer_complaint_narrative:
The 3 CRA 'S are wrongfully reporting several inquiries on my credit report that I do not recognize nor authorized. I am writing to inform the CRAs to delete these erroneous inquiries. As they are violating my consumer rights governed by the fcra. 

I am writing to file a complaint regarding violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) by XXXX, EXPERIAN, AND XXXX. I believe that the CRA 's have failed to comply with several provisions of the FCRA in its handling of my credit report, including the following sections : Section 604 - This section requires CRAs to provide consumers with a copy of their credit report upon request.

Section 609 - This section requires CRAs to provide consumers with a notice of their rights under the FCRA when they receive a copy of their credit report.

Section 611 - This section requires CRAs to investigate consumer disputes and to correct or delete inaccurate or incomplete information in their credit reports.

Section 615 - This section requires CRAs to follow reasonable procedures to ensure the maximum possible accuracy of the information in credit reports.

Section 617 - This section provides consumers with a private right of action to sue CRAs and other parties that violate the FCRA.

Section 623 - This section requires users of credit reports to provide notice to consumers before taking adverse action based on information in a credit report.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), Section 623 sets out the responsibilities of credit reporting agencies ( CRAs ) and furnishers of credit information with respect to the accuracy and completeness of credit information. Some of the relevant subsections of Section 623 include : 623 ( a ) ( 1 ), which requires CRAs to maintain reasonable procedures to ensure the maximum possible accuracy of the information in their credit reports.

623 ( a ) ( 2 ), which requires furnishers of credit information to provide complete and accurate information to CRAs.

Consumer_complaint_narrative:
On XX/XX/2020, I noticed that I had lost my credit card. I immediately reported it lost and requested a new credit card from Bank of America. I received e-mail notification that a new card would be mailed to me. I did not receive one, and Bank of America did not put a freeze on the account. 

On XX/XX/2020, after the XXXX holiday, I logged into my Bank of America account online. There were in store charges in excess of {$3000.00} made during the holiday week on the card. I promptly called to report the fraud, to understand why the account had not been frozen, and why I had never received a new card in the mail. They were very apologetic, froze the account, and issued a new credit card number. They also opened a fraud dispute and temporarily credited my account. 

After 30 days, I received a notice saying that my fraud claim was denied because I had made purchases at these vendors in the past. However, that is not true. Whoever had my card spent ~ {$2000.00} at XXXX XXXX, which I had not been to in recent memory. In addition, {$600.00} at XXXX, and my phone provider was XXXX at the time. I explained the facts again, and the fraud agent opened an appeal case. 

After 30 additional days, I received a second notice that the claim was denied for the same reason. I called once more, and explained the facts. I did not have the card in my possession, as I had reported it lost prior to any of these in store purchases. The fraud agent then instructed me to file a police report, which I had not been instructed to do until this time. 

I then filed a local police report, and submitted it to the fraud department. Some time later, I received yet another notice that the claim was denied for the same reason as the first two times. 

Ultimately, I ended up paying for the fraudulent charges because it would be too expensive to hire legal counsel. It is aggravating that a very reputable financial institution would handle a fraud claim in this manner. I have since transitioned my core banking to a local credit union, and will soon close all accounts held with Bank of America because of how this claim was handled two years ago. I was recently made aware that I could file a complaint with the CFPB so that at least my experience would be on the record.

Consumer_complaint_narrative:
Wells Fargo advertises that they may make funds available for direct deposit payroll checks two days early for payroll checks, pensions, and government assistance checks. 
Since XX/XX/23, I have received my payroll check two days early into my account. I work for a government agency. Due to this, I was under the impression that would be the process going forward. I then scheduled bill payments based on this. This is a pay week for me and I believed the money would be in my account on XX/XX/23 as they have practiced this in the past. The actual pay date is XX/XX/23. On XX/XX/23, the money was not applied and I incurred overdraft fees based on the bill pay I had scheduled. On XX/XX/23, I contacted the Wells Fargo Customer service line and spoke with an agent. The agent stated that the two day early funds program is not guaranteed and is not always available. I understand that and the same verbiage is listed on their website, however this a is payroll check from a government agency in which the funds have already been sent. There is no difference in the account of where the payroll check is coming from nor is the amount different. I am paid the same amount every two weeks. It is not best practice to allow early deposits on some payroll deposits and not others on the same customer account. I asked for the overdraft fees to be reduced and the agent would only give a partial credit. When I ask for a supervisor, the agent stated that they could send it for another review while I was on the phone with them. Then the agent came back and credited the entire amount. Wells Fargo continues to enter into deceptive practices that marginalize those who make minimum wages and struggle to pay bills. I plan my bill paying around the days when I have seen the funds available. I will tell you I will never make that mistake again, nor will I rely on Wells Fargo to make my funds available early. At this point, they are making it look like they are helping their customers by offering early pay day but that is not what is truly happening. If I had not pushed to speak to a supervisor and accepted the partial credit, Wells Fargo would have profited off the mistakes I made due to believing that they are truly doing the right thing with their customers by offering early bill pay. Consumers should be educated on this practice and how it can be deceptive since Wells Fargo picks and chooses at their leisure to provide a consumer with the funds early or not. There needs to be a standard that is followed to see that once a consumer receives funds early, this would be the case with every payroll check going forward.

rescission of contract To abrogate, annul, avoid, or cancel a contract ; particularly, nullifying a contract by the act of either party. The right of rescission is the right to cancel ( rescind ) a contract upon the occurrence of certain kinds of default by the other contracting party. To declare a contract void in its inception and to put an end to it as though it never were. Russell v. Stephens, 191 Wash. 314, 71 P.2d 30, 31.

A " rescission '' amounts to the unmaking of a contract, or an undoing of it from the beginning, and not merely a termination, and it may be effected by mutual agreement of parties, or by one of the parties declaring rescission of contract without consent of other if a legally sufficient ground therefor exists, or by applying to courts for a decree of rescission. Abdallah , Inc. v. Martin, 242 Minn. 416, 65 N.W.2d 641, 644. 
It necessarily involves a repudiation of the contract and a refusal of the moving party to be further bound by it. 

An action of an equitable nature in which a party seeks to be relieved of his obligations under a contract on the grounds of mutual mistake, fraud, impossibility, etc. It does not require permission from either party.
